entries.answer: The scientific method is the procedure that makes a claim checkable by other people, and its structure is a cycle rather than a straight line: observation, question, hypothesis, experiment, analysis, and back to the start, because a result that contradicts the hypothesis sends you round again rather than ending the enquiry. The parts that are genuinely required are that the claim is stated so it could be wrong, that the test is a fair test of that specific claim, and that the result is reported whatever it was. Publishing the method along with the result is what allows someone else to repeat it, which is why replication rather than plausibility is the real currency, and why a claim with no stated method is not yet a scientific claim at all. A method can be wrong without anyone lying, and a good course in research methods spends most of its time on the ways that happens: an unrepresentative sample, a measurement that changes what it is supposed to measure, and a conclusion that claims more than the design can support. The method does not tell you which theory is true; it tells you which claims have survived being tested.

patterns: what is variable in an experiment
definition of variable in an experiment
what is a variable in an experiment
entries.answer: A variable in an experiment is any quantity that can change and might affect the result, and the discipline of designing a study is mostly the discipline of deciding which ones to control. The independent variable is the one the researcher deliberately changes, the dependent variable is the outcome being measured, and everything else that could also change the outcome is a confounding variable and has to be held constant or accounted for. A study that changes a supplement and measures blood pressure has an independent variable of the supplement, a dependent variable of blood pressure, and confounders of diet, exercise, stress and time of day, and if those are not handled then a result cannot be attributed to the supplement. Randomisation is the tool that handles unmeasured confounders, because assigning participants at random balances them on average, and it is why a randomised trial is the strongest design available. The related distinction is between a variable you record and a variable you change: an observation is what you are measuring, and a manipulation is what you are doing to it, and a correlational study only ever does the first, which is why it cannot establish that one thing caused another.

entries.answer: Quantum mechanics describes matter and energy at very small scales, where particles behave in ways everyday intuition gets wrong. A quantum state can be a superposition of several possibilities at once until it is measured, and two particles can be entangled so that measuring one instantly constrains the other, however far apart. It is not a guess - it is the most precisely tested theory in physics, and it is what gives us semiconductors and lasers.
